---
title: "Concentration of S&P 500 index"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE)
```

In this data challege we study how concentrated the S&P 500 is among its constituent companies.

1. The S&P 500 (Standard & Poor's 500) is a stock market index that tracks the performance of 500 of the largest publicly traded companies in the United States.
2. It covers roughly 80% of the total value of the U.S. stock market.
3. It is a market-capitalization-weighted index. Larger companies have a much bigger impact on its value than smaller components


We will use:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidyquant)
library(ineq)
```

The three packages have different roles:

```text
tidyquant    retrieve the S&P 500 constituents and weights
tidyverse    manipulate and visualize the data
ineq         calculate the Lorenz curve and Gini coefficient
```

Our main questions are:

1. How unequal are the company weights in the S&P 500?

```{r}
sp500 <- tq_index("SP500")

# weights sorted from the largest to the smallest
weights <- sp500 |>
  filter(weight > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(weight))

# the 10 largest companies by weight
weights |>
  select(symbol, company, weight) |>
  head(10)

# share of the index held by the top 10 companies
sum(weights$weight[1:10]) / sum(weights$weight)

ggplot(weights) +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = weight * 100), binwidth = 0.1) +
  labs(x = "weight (%)", y = "number of companies")

# Lorenz curve of the weights
lc <- Lc(weights$weight)
lorenz <- tibble(p = lc$p, L = lc$L)

ggplot(lorenz) +
  geom_line(aes(x = p, y = L)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "cumulative share of companies",
       y = "cumulative share of index weight")
```

2. How much of the index is represented by its largest companies?

```{r}
# share of the index held by the n largest companies
cumulative <- tibble(
  rank = 1:nrow(weights),
  share = cumsum(weights$weight) / sum(weights$weight)
)

cumulative |>
  filter(rank %in% c(1, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100))

ggplot(cumulative) +
  geom_line(aes(x = rank, y = share * 100)) +
  labs(x = "number of largest companies",
       y = "cumulative share of the index (%)")

# smallest number of companies holding at least half of the index
cumulative |>
  filter(share >= 0.5) |>
  head(1) |>
  mutate(fraction_of_companies = rank / nrow(cumulative))
```

3. What does the Lorenz curve tell us about concentration?

```{r}
# share of the index held by the smallest x% of companies
bottom_share <- function(x) {
  lorenz$L[lorenz$p >= x][1]
}

bottom_share(0.5)       # smallest 50%
bottom_share(0.8)       # smallest 80%
1 - bottom_share(0.9)   # largest 10%
1 - bottom_share(0.99)  # largest 1%

ggplot(lorenz) +
  geom_line(aes(x = p, y = L)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted") +
  labs(x = "cumulative share of companies (smallest first)",
       y = "cumulative share of index weight")
```

4. What is the Gini coefficient of the S&P 500 weights?

```{r}
# Gini coefficient: 0 = perfect equality, 1 = one company holds everything
Gini(weights$weight)

# Gini without the 10 largest companies
Gini(weights$weight[-(1:10)])
```
